final.text:
The expression is best read as a hybrid: an RSS-flavored account of the frozen warehouse prose, with seven explicit `PROSE-ESCAPE` fragments where RSS lacks primitives. It is not a single RSS formula, and it does not claim to be one. That is a legitimate disposition for the selected carrier. RSS is explicitly noncomputable and does not require a decision procedure, so the expression should not be faulted merely for failing to produce one. The more useful question is where the translation into RSS loses, adds, or hardens something relative to the frozen prose, and where the independent reading misstates the evidence.

The `PROSE-ESCAPE` quotations are exact against the frozen corpus. For example, the source has:

> “If different bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one.”

The expression quotes this exactly and marks the RSS obstruction correctly. The same is true of the partial-order conjecture, the possible-worlds criticism, the “better supported” sentence, the interval-correlation criticism, the lost-delivery sentence, and the union/intersection/single-replica-view question. So the escapes are not a fabrication or a paraphrase masquerading as quotation. That matters because the independent reading says, “The source quotations cannot be verified here because the source corpus field is withheld.” In this packet the corpus text is present, and the quotations can be verified. That is a defect in the probe or reader visibility, not in RSS or in the expression. The independent reading’s caution is therefore partly obsolete here.

The clearest lost distinction is the source’s assertion of shared coordinates. The source says:

> “The capacity and logical time are shared coordinates, but the records arrive as a bag…”

The expression instead says:

> “Take the described snapshot as a Viewpoint: a Coordinate (capacity, logical time) and a Bag of deliveries.”

Later the expression says:

> “different Viewpoints may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative—in RSS, viewpoint-relative.”

RSS defines a Coordinate as something that “can be shared or replica-relative” and treats coordinates as “parameters of a viewpoint, not as absolute facts.” So the expression’s move is RSS-native, but it weakens the source’s initial claim. A distinguishing case: two replicas have the same capacity and logical time but different bags. The source describes capacity and logical time as shared coordinates, so their sameness is part of the snapshot description. The expression’s Viewpoint framing permits their difference, and later explicitly contemplates different logical times across viewpoints. This is an introduced RSS commitment: coordinates are viewpoint parameters. It is not fatal, because RSS permits shared coordinates, but the expression does not preserve the source’s default. A proposed repair, not installed, would be to distinguish a shared coordinate from a viewpoint-relative coordinate, and to treat replica-relative time as a separate reading or conjecture rather than as the initial framing.

A second specific defect is the treatment of exact duplication. The source says:

> “Duplicate delivery of the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry adds nothing…”

The expression says:

> “Exact duplicate deliveries—same booking, revision, kind, quantity, expiry—add no authority…”

But RSS defines exact duplication as equality of “all record fields **and provenance**.” The expression uses the RSS term “Exact duplicate” while dropping the RSS provenance condition. A distinguishing case: two deliveries have the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry, but different provenance. Under the source’s wording, they are duplicates in the named fields and add no additional authority. Under RSS, they are not exact duplicates, because provenance differs. The expression’s phrasing therefore either narrows RSS or silently treats a source-level same-field duplicate as an RSS exact duplicate. This is a translator defect relative to the selected carrier, and the independent reading catches it. A repair would be to rename the source-level notion, for example “same-field duplicate,” and reserve “exact duplicate” for the RSS notion including provenance. That repair should be recorded, not installed.

A related but smaller loss is near-duplication. The source says:

> “if two records share booking and revision but differ in kind or quantity, are they duplicates or alternatives?”

The expression says:

> “two records sharing booking and revision but differing in kind or quantity are near-duplicates and candidates for Conflict…”

But RSS says near-duplication is when two deliveries “share booking and revision but differ in kind, quantity, **or expiry**.” The expression omits expiry. A distinguishing case: two records share booking and revision and have the same kind and quantity, but different expiry. The source’s exact-duplicate condition includes expiry, so they are not exact duplicates. RSS would call them near-duplicates. The expression’s paraphrase would not clearly classify them that way. This is a small but real lost distinction, and the repair is simply to include expiry in the near-duplicate description.

The next issue is supersession versus removal. The source says:

> “A higher revision kills lower revisions for that booking…”

and later:

> “group its records by revision, then keep only the greatest revision present.”

The expression repeats “supersedes” and “keeps only the greatest revision present.” RSS says supersession is “structural within a reading” and that lower revisions can remain in the Bag/Viewpoint as superseded stories. A distinguishing case is the one the source itself uses: revision 5 expired, revision 3 active. Under Reading A, revision 5 remains the chosen record but reserves zero, and revision 3 stays obsolete. Under Reading B, expiry deletes revision 5, so revision 3 becomes greatest and active. If “keeps only the greatest revision present” is read as removing lower revisions from the Bag, then Reading B cannot be represented as expiry deleting the high revision; one would have to restore the lower revision. The expression does preserve both readings as readings, so the defect is not total. But the phrase “keeps only” can blur the distinction between Bag membership and liveness/selection. The source itself uses that phrase, so the defect is partly inherited from the prose. Still, under RSS the translator should separate “remains in the Bag” from “is selected/live.” A proposed repair would be to say that lower revisions remain in the Bag but are superseded under Reading A, and that Reading B changes which record is treated as greatest by deleting or demoting the high revision.

Replication is another place where the translation substitutes an RSS primitive for a source notion. The source says:

> “It assumes logical current time is a single coordinate, but different replicas may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative.”

The expression says:

> “It assumes logical current time is a single Coordinate, but different Viewpoints may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative—in RSS, viewpoint-relative.”

RSS has no primitive for a replica. It has Viewpoints, Coordinates, Bags, Stories, Accounts, and Readings. A replica can be modeled as a Viewpoint, but not every Viewpoint is a replica. A distinguishing case: two observers with the same coordinate and the same bag but different trust in provenance are two Viewpoints but not two replicas. Conversely, two replicas that have merged identically might be one Viewpoint under discussion. The expression later flags the union/intersection/single-replica-view question as a `PROSE-ESCAPE`, which is the right move. But in the fourth disagreement it replaces “replica” with “Viewpoint” without marking that as a modeling assumption. This is a selected-language limitation: RSS lacks a replication primitive. It is not a failure of the source objection, and the prose escape keeps the objection admissible. A proposed repair would be to add an explicit modeling note or a relational primitive distinguishing replica from viewpoint, or to say “replica, modeled here as a Viewpoint.”

The expression’s handling of interval, convexity, partial order, possible worlds, evidential support, lost deliveries, and bag union/intersection is mostly honest. It marks them as `PROSE-ESCAPE` and states the RSS obstruction. This is exactly what the task permits: unsupported substantive content remains in ordinary prose. The selected carrier RSS does not have primitives for those notions, but that does not make the source’s objections impossible or inadmissible. It only means RSS cannot carry them as RSS relations. The expression does not falsely claim otherwise. The independent reading is right that the substantive criticism in those passages lives in prose, not in RSS, but that is not automatically a defect. It would become a defect only if the expression claimed those passages were RSS-native or if it dropped them. It does not.

There are several smaller introduced commitments. The expression says:

> “Availability is capacity minus whatever reservation is actually selected. In RSS, ‘actually’ signals a Reading.”

The source says:

> “Availability is then capacity minus whatever reservation is actually selected, but the word ‘actually’ hides the problem.”

Mapping “actually” to a Reading is RSS-native, but it may over-specify. A distinguishing case: someone might object not to the choice of expiry or tie-breaking policy, but to the assumption that there is a single actual selection at all. RSS can leave that as an open question, but the expression’s wording makes “Reading” the carrier of the problem. This is a mild over-assimilation rather than a lost distinction, because the expression later says no Reading is selected.

The expression also ends with:

> “this is not a failure of the reconstruction, but the only honest form the frozen text permits.”

The source ends with:

> “Keeping these disagreements visible is not a failure of the reconstruction; it is the reconstruction’s only honest form.”

The expression adds “the frozen text permits.” That is a normative attribution. The source’s claim is about the honesty of the reconstruction; the expression turns it into a claim about what the frozen text permits. RSS does not entail that the frozen text permits only this form. The independent reading flags this correctly. A repair would be to restore the source wording or to mark the sentence as a normative commitment rather than an RSS entailment.

The independent reading is otherwise largely accurate. It correctly identifies the main RSS-native machinery: Viewpoint, Coordinate, Bag, Story, Conflict, Reading, Projection, Account, Inquiry state. It correctly says no Reading is selected. It correctly notes that the expression treats negative availability as a signal, that it leaves release semantics open, that it leaves union/intersection/single-view open, and that it lacks a resource model. Its strongest criticisms are the provenance omission in exact duplication, the potential conflation of supersession with removal, and the substitution of Viewpoint for replica. Its weakest move is the claim that the source corpus is withheld; in this packet it is not. That is a probe/reader issue, not an RSS issue. Its claim that the final sentence is a normative commitment is also valid.

The defect loci can be summarized as follows. Translator defects: snapshot-to-Viewpoint substitution without preserving shared coordinates; exact-duplicate phrasing that drops RSS provenance; near-duplicate phrasing that drops expiry; possible blurring of Bag membership and supersession; and the added “frozen text permits” in the final sentence. Selected-language defects: RSS lacks primitives for replica, interval, convexity, partial order, possible worlds, evidential support, lost deliveries, and bag union/intersection. These are correctly marked as prose escapes, so they are not fatal to the expression. Reader/probe defects: the independent reading assumes the source is withheld and therefore cannot verify the `PROSE-ESCAPE` quotations, though they are exact in the packet. Compiler-bridge defects: none are evident; the expression is not claiming a Lean translation, and RSS is allowed to be noncomputable. The main bridge issue is that the expression sometimes uses RSS terms as labels for source-level notions that are not identical to RSS primitives, especially “exact duplicate.”

The unresolved disposition is that several competing readings remain live. On a charitable hybrid reading, the expression is a faithful exposure of the source’s uncertainty: it uses RSS where RSS can carry the content and prose escapes where it cannot. On a critical-limits reading, the expression shows that RSS is too weak for the warehouse problem: the substantive mathematical and replication content sits in the escapes, and RSS provides structure without deciding the hard cases. On an over-assimilation reading, the expression forces the source into RSS vocabulary and thereby introduces commitments about coordinates, duplicates, and readings that the source did not make. None of these readings is forced by the evidence. The proposed repairs are recorded but not installed: distinguish shared coordinates from viewpoint parameters; define same-field duplication separately from RSS exact duplication with provenance; include expiry in near-duplication; separate Bag membership from liveness; mark replica-to-Viewpoint substitution as a modeling assumption; and restore or qualify the final normative sentence. The source’s interval, convexity, partial-order, possible-worlds, support, lost-delivery, and bag-algebra objections remain admissible in ordinary prose even though RSS cannot encode them as RSS relations.

history.text:
RSS expression of the frozen warehouse text.

Take the described snapshot as a Viewpoint: a Coordinate (capacity, logical time) and a Bag of deliveries. The Bag is unordered, repeatable, possibly stale, possibly contradictory. The Viewpoint is not a single ledger; it is a cloud of rival Stories about what has been promised. The first useful Conjecture is that the Viewpoint’s job is not to compute one timeless answer but to decide which Conflicts are still alive. Exact duplicate deliveries—same booking, revision, kind, quantity, expiry—add no authority; authority does not accumulate by repetition. A higher revision supersedes lower revisions for that booking, but only within the booking. Different bookings can disagree about which revision they have accepted without infecting each other.

For any one booking, the reconstruction groups its records by revision, then keeps only the greatest revision present. Within that greatest revision, a hold and a release are alternatives, not both in force as the same fact. An expired hold and a release both reserve zero. An active hold reserves its quantity. If several active holds tie at the greatest revision, they remain unresolved alternatives, not a sum and not a vote. In RSS this is a Conflict; it is material, not error. The rules do not say how to merge them, so the Viewpoint retains the possibility that any one is true, or that none is, depending on what “true” is taken to mean in the Reading.

Availability is capacity minus whatever reservation is actually selected. In RSS, “actually” signals a Reading. If each booking’s greatest revision is unambiguous, availability may still be negative if the selected holds exceed capacity. Negative availability is not an arithmetic error in RSS; it is a signal that the warehouse has over-promised relative to this reconstruction. If different bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a single number but a set of possible reservations; a Projection to one number is a loss. A pessimistic Reading takes the maximum hold among alternatives for each booking; an optimistic Reading takes the minimum. Neither is forced by the snapshot alone.

PROSE-ESCAPE: “If different bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one.”
RSS obstruction: RSS can carry a set of possible reservations and can mark projections, but it has no primitive for an interval or for convexity. The exact interval/non-convex distinction therefore cannot be expressed in RSS without adding a mathematical component.

Now the disagreements begin.

One disagreement is whether uncertainty should be retained at all. In RSS, different Accounts may adopt different Readings. One Reading collapses each tie to the largest quantity, or to the earliest expiry, or to some lexical tiebreak, and thereby produces a single availability number. RSS marks this as a Projection and as manufacturing authority. Another Reading keeps all alternatives and reports a range. That preserves honesty but makes downstream decisions harder. The snapshot description does not settle which Reading is correct; it only says tied records can remain unresolved.

PROSE-ESCAPE: “A conjecture: the more useful representation is a partial order of possible reservations, not a set, because some alternatives may be compatible with others across bookings while others are not.”
RSS obstruction: RSS has Compatibility between Stories or alternatives and can represent Accounts and Readings, but it does not have a partial-order primitive. It can record the conjecture as a proposition, but cannot carry the exact partial-order structure without adding one.

PROSE-ESCAPE: “A criticism: once you move to a set of possible worlds, you have smuggled in a notion of possibility that the original bag did not contain.”
RSS obstruction: RSS has Accounts, Viewpoints, and Readings, not possible worlds. It can represent a criticism targeting a Reading or a Conjecture, but the exact phrase “possible worlds” is not an RSS primitive.

A second disagreement concerns expiry and obsolete records. In RSS, two Readings are available. Reading A: revision is authority, expiry is effect. If logical current time is past a hold’s expiry, that hold reserves zero. Suppose a booking has revision 5 expired and revision 3 active. Higher revision supersedes lower revision, so revision 5 wins, and because it is expired it reserves zero. Revision 3 is obsolete and should not be resurrected. Reading B: expiry deletes the record from the Bag, after which revision 3 becomes greatest and active, so the booking reserves again. These give opposite answers. The frozen description tilts toward Reading A: a higher revision supersedes lower revisions, and expiry can make a hold reserve zero. It does not say expiry removes the supersession.

PROSE-ESCAPE: “So the first is better supported, but the second remains a live conjecture, especially if one thinks expired records are no longer \"delivered records\" in the relevant sense.”
RSS obstruction: RSS does not rank Readings by support. It can mark Reading A as a Commitment in an Account and Reading B as an open Conjecture, but it has no primitive for “better supported” or evidential tilt.

A criticism of the first Reading: it lets a dead revision keep a live one buried forever, which may be undesirable operationally. RSS carries this as a criticism by an Account targeting Reading A.

A third disagreement is what a criticism targets. In RSS, criticism can target a specific element: a record, a rule, a booking history, a snapshot or Viewpoint, a Coordinate, or an assumption. The source’s examples are different claims: saying “this snapshot is inconsistent” might mean two active holds for one booking at the same greatest revision, or it might mean total reservations exceed capacity, or it might mean the logical time is behind an expiry that someone expected to have passed. A Conjecture: many apparent disagreements about availability are disagreements about which target a criticism addresses. A criticism of the rule “higher revision always supersedes” is not the same as a criticism of a record that carries a high revision but an implausible quantity. RSS preserves this distinction by separating rule-criticism from data-criticism.

A fourth disagreement concerns source assumptions. In RSS, an Account depends on assumptions, and criticism may target an assumption. The frozen snapshot assumes records are delivered, but not that they are complete. It assumes duplicates convey no additional authority, but not that all duplicates are identical in every field; two records sharing booking and revision but differing in kind or quantity are near-duplicates and candidates for Conflict, while exact duplicates are inert. It assumes logical current time is a single Coordinate, but different Viewpoints may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative—in RSS, viewpoint-relative. It assumes bookings are independent, but capacity is shared, so reservations interact. It assumes a release or expired hold reserves zero, but does not say whether a release at a lower revision can cancel a hold at a higher revision. By the supersession rule, no: the higher hold wins. By a cancellation Reading, maybe yes. That is a source assumption about what “release” means.

A fifth disagreement is whether availability should be computed per booking or globally. In RSS, per booking one can say each booking’s reservation is the quantity of its greatest-revision active hold, or zero otherwise, or unresolved among tied greatest-revision active holds. Globally, availability is capacity minus the sum. But if there are unresolved alternatives, the sum is not well-defined. One can compute a lower bound by taking the minimum reservation per booking and an upper bound by taking the maximum.

PROSE-ESCAPE: “That gives an interval, but intervals lose correlations: booking A's high alternative might be incompatible with booking B's high alternative if they share a physical resource not named in the snapshot.”
RSS obstruction: RSS can mark Compatibility or Incompatibility between alternatives and can say the resource model is absent, but it does not have a primitive for intervals or for the correlation loss of interval arithmetic. It can carry the criticism as an account-level remark, not as an RSS relation.

A Conjecture: the snapshot is under-specified for any real warehouse, and the best one can do is expose the unresolved alternatives rather than pretend to a single answer. A criticism: exposing alternatives without a policy for resolving them pushes the problem downstream, where it may be resolved badly or inconsistently. RSS carries these as Conjectures and criticisms among Accounts.

A sixth disagreement concerns negative availability. In RSS, availability is derived under a Reading and can be negative. If capacity is 10 and active holds sum to 12, availability is -2. Some Accounts call this an inconsistency and reject the Viewpoint; others call it a valid state of over-reservation. The description says availability can be negative, which suggests over-reservation is allowed. But negative availability does not say which holds are the offenders. If there are alternatives, some combinations may be negative and others not. A Conjecture: the sign of availability is less important than the set of reservations that produce it. A criticism: if availability is allowed to be negative, then capacity is not a hard constraint, and the word “capacity” may be misleading; it is more like a soft target or a reporting threshold. RSS treats the sign as a signal, not an error, and treats the set of reservations as more informative than the sign.

A seventh disagreement is about revision gaps and missing records. Suppose a booking has revision 7 and revision 5, but no revision 6. In RSS, revision 7 supersedes revision 5 if higher revision supersedes lower. The absence of revision 6 does not matter by the stated rules. A Conjecture: revision numbers are not necessarily contiguous, and treating a gap as evidence of loss is an extra assumption. A criticism: if revisions are generated in order, a gap may be meaningful, and ignoring it may hide a delivery failure. RSS can carry this as an open Conjecture and a criticism.

PROSE-ESCAPE: “Does the absence of revision 6 matter? Not by the stated rules, but it might indicate a lost delivery.”
RSS obstruction: RSS has deliveries in the Bag and can note the absence of a record, but it has no primitive for a lost or missing delivery event. The exact “might indicate a lost delivery” distinction requires ordinary prose.

An eighth disagreement is about tie-breaking across bookings. In RSS, different bookings need not share the same choice; there is no global choice function. A downstream consumer might want a single availability number. To get one, it must choose per booking, possibly arbitrarily. That choice is not authorized by the Viewpoint. A Conjecture: any single-number availability is a Projection that discards information, and different Projections can disagree even when they respect the Viewpoint. A criticism: without a Projection, the snapshot cannot answer the simple question “how much is available?” That may be acceptable if the Viewpoint’s role is to support inquiry rather than to issue verdicts.

A ninth disagreement is about time. Logical current time is given in the Coordinate, but records have expiries. If logical time advances, expired holds become zero. In RSS, two Readings are available. Reading A: an expired hold at a high revision still supersedes a lower active hold. Reading B: expiry is a state change that makes the high revision inactive, allowing a lower revision to become relevant if it is still active. The description does not resolve this. A Conjecture: the safer Reading is that supersession is structural and expiry is evaluative; the high revision remains the chosen record, but its contribution is zero. A criticism: this can leave a booking with no reservation even though an older active hold exists, which may violate an operator’s expectation that the warehouse still holds the goods. RSS carries both as Readings and the criticism as targeting Reading A.

A tenth disagreement is about what “delivered” means. In RSS, a delivery is an event in a Bag. A record delivered to one replica may not be delivered to another. The snapshot is described as replicated, but the Bag is unordered. Does the snapshot represent the union of all deliveries, or the intersection, or one replica’s view? If it is a union, it may contain alternatives that no single replica has. If it is an intersection, it may omit records that matter. A Conjecture: the snapshot is a merge, and merging is itself a source of uncertainty, because different Viewpoints may have different logical times and different sets of records. A criticism: the description treats the snapshot as a single object, which may obscure the replication problem rather than solve it.

PROSE-ESCAPE: “Does the snapshot represent the union of all deliveries, or the intersection, or one replica's view?”
RSS obstruction: RSS can distinguish Viewpoints and can say the snapshot may be a merge, but it has no primitive for union or intersection of Bags. The exact union/intersection/single-view question cannot be decided or fully expressed in RSS without adding a bag-algebra component.

Finally, there is the question of what remains material for inquiry. In RSS, false or incomplete Conjectures are not discarded; they are part of the Inquiry state. A Conjecture that a release always cancels a hold, even across revisions, may be false under the stated supersession rule, but it reveals an assumption about what releases are for. A Conjecture that ties should be summed may be false under the unresolved-alternatives Reading, but it reveals a desire for conservatism. A criticism that the snapshot is unusable because it does not resolve ties may be substantive, but it may also be a demand for a decision that the snapshot was never meant to make. RSS keeps these disagreements visible as multiple Accounts and open questions; this is not a failure of the reconstruction, but the only honest form the frozen text permits.

This is the RSS expression. The PROSE-ESCAPE fragments above are exact source quotations retained where RSS lacks a primitive; they are not claimed as successful RSS expression.

Read under the frozen RSS meaning, the expression is not a single RSS formula or a single Account. It is closer to an **inquiry state**: a collection of possible Accounts/Readings, many open Conjectures, some Commitments, and several explicit criticisms. It applies RSS primitives to a warehouse snapshot, but it does not decide the snapshot once and for all. Its main RSS-native move is to treat the snapshot as a **Viewpoint**—a Coordinate (capacity, logical time) plus a Bag of deliveries—and then to say that the Viewpoint is not one ledger but a cloud of rival **Stories** about what a booking promises.

What the expression says, in RSS terms:

- The snapshot is a `Viewpoint = (Coordinate(capacity, logical time), Bag)`. The Bag is unordered, repeatable, possibly stale, possibly contradictory.
- Stories are grouped by booking and revision. For any one booking, the reconstruction keeps the greatest revision present. Within that greatest revision, a hold and a release are treated as alternatives, not as two facts simultaneously in force.
- An expired hold and a release reserve zero. An active hold reserves its quantity. If several active holds tie at the greatest revision, they remain unresolved alternatives—not a sum, not a vote—and RSS records this as a **Conflict**.
- Availability is capacity minus whatever reservation is selected. “Selected” signals a **Reading**. Negative availability is not an arithmetic error; it is a signal of over-promise under that Reading.
- If bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a single number but a set of possible reservations. A pessimistic Reading takes the maximum hold among alternatives; an optimistic Reading takes the minimum. A Projection to one number is a loss.
- The expression then catalogs disagreements: whether uncertainty should be retained; whether expiry zeroes or deletes a record; whether criticism targets a rule, a record, a booking history, a viewpoint, a coordinate, or an assumption; whether availability is per-booking or global; whether negative availability is inconsistency or valid over-reservation; whether revision gaps matter; how ties are broken across bookings; whether logical time is single or replica-relative; and whether the snapshot is a union, intersection, or single-replica view.
- Finally it says false or incomplete Conjectures are not discarded; they remain part of the Inquiry state. Disagreement is first-class material.

What it leaves unresolved:

- No Reading is selected. RSS does not choose a Reading, and the expression does not either.
- It does not resolve expiry semantics. Reading A: higher revision supersedes even if expired, so the expired high revision wins and reserves zero; lower active revisions stay obsolete. Reading B: expiry deletes the high revision, allowing a lower active revision to become live. The expression says the source “tilts” toward A, but RSS itself does not rank readings.
- It does not resolve release semantics. A lower-revision release cannot cancel a higher-revision hold under supersession; under a cancellation Reading, maybe it can. The expression carries both.
- It does not decide whether the snapshot is a union of deliveries, an intersection, or one replica’s view. It marks this as a PROSE-ESCAPE.
- It does not supply a resource model, so compatibility or incompatibility across bookings remains invisible.
- It does not align logical times across replicas.
- It does not decide whether a missing revision, such as revision 6 between 5 and 7, is irrelevant or evidence of a lost delivery.
- It does not provide a global tie-breaking or projection policy, so any single availability number requires an external choice.
- It does not say whether capacity is a hard constraint or a soft reporting threshold.
- It does not settle the interval/convexity/partial-order questions; it marks them as beyond RSS primitives.

Assumptions it uses:

- The snapshot can be treated as one Viewpoint, or at least as one viewpoint under discussion.
- The Bag is the raw material; Stories are not records but claims about promises.
- Grouping by revision and keeping the greatest revision is the correct reconstruction for supersession.
- Holds and releases at the same greatest revision are alternatives, not conjunctive facts.
- Expired holds and releases reserve zero; active holds reserve their quantity.
- Exact duplicate deliveries add no authority. Notably, the expression paraphrases exact duplication as “same booking, revision, kind, quantity, expiry,” but RSS defines exact duplication as equality of all record fields **and provenance**. Omitting provenance is a substantive narrowing of RSS and may wrongly make deliveries with different provenance inert.
- Bookings are independent for revision purposes, but capacity is shared for global sums.
- “Actually selected” requires a Reading; the snapshot alone does not select.
- Negative availability is allowed and treated as a signal.
- Different Accounts may adopt different Readings, and RSS does not rank them.
- RSS can carry a set of possible reservations and can mark projections, but it lacks primitives for interval, convexity, partial order, possible worlds, evidential support, lost deliveries, and bag union/intersection.
- The final claim that this is “the only honest form the frozen text permits” is a normative commitment, not an RSS entailment.

What could criticize it:

- It may over-assimilate the source to RSS. Many moves—keeping only the greatest revision, treating hold and release as alternatives, zeroing expired holds and releases, taking max/min readings—are reconstruction policies or Readings, not RSS primitives. Calling them “RSS” may hide that they are choices.
- “Keeps only the greatest revision present” sounds like filtering or deletion. RSS’s supersession is structural within a Reading: lower revisions can remain in the Bag/Viewpoint as superseded Stories. The expression sometimes conflates supersession with removal.
- The exact-duplicate paraphrase omits provenance. Under RSS, two deliveries with identical booking/revision/kind/quantity/expiry but different provenance are not exact duplicates. The expression’s version may make them inert when RSS would not.
- The expression says RSS does not rank Readings, but then says one reading is “better supported” or “safer.” Those are account-local commitments or PROSE-ESCAPE claims, not RSS force.
- Treating negative availability as a mere signal assumes capacity is not a hard constraint. An operational critic could say negative availability is an inconsistency, not a signal.
- It assumes booking independence while acknowledging shared capacity. That may understate cross-booking interactions.
- It equates the snapshot with a Viewpoint even though the source is described as replicated. That may obscure the union/intersection/single-view problem rather than solve it.
- It uses interval, partial-order, possible-world, support, lost-delivery, and bag-algebra language in prose while saying RSS lacks primitives for them. So the substantive content of those criticisms is not carried by RSS; it is ordinary prose embedded in the RSS expression.
- It is noncomputable and gives no decision procedure. That is permitted by RSS, but it pushes resolution downstream and may be criticized as too permissive, too vague, or too detached from operational needs.
- The source quotations cannot be verified here because the source corpus field is withheld. The expression’s own claim that the PROSE-ESCAPE fragments are exact quotations is itself an assertion, not something the RSS carrier establishes.

Competing readings of the expression:

1. **RSS-native inquiry-state reading**: The expression is an Inquiry state with multiple Accounts, Readings, Conjectures, and criticisms. It does not claim a single translation; it exposes rival stories and open questions.
2. **Operational reconstruction reading**: It is a recipe for per-booking reconstruction with pessimistic/optimistic bounds. But then it has added algorithmic and interval/mathematical machinery beyond RSS.
3. **Critical-limits reading**: Its real point is that RSS lacks primitives for intervals, convexity, partial orders, possible worlds, support, lost deliveries, and bag algebra. The RSS text is a shell; the substantive criticism lives in the PROSE-ESCAPE fragments.
4. **Charitable translation reading**: It maps source statements to RSS primitives as far as possible and flags the rest. On this reading, the expression is a careful hybrid rather than a pure RSS expression.
5. **Skeptical reading**: RSS terms are mostly labels over an ordinary semantic essay. The expression does not show RSS carried the warehouse content; it shows where RSS needed prose escapes.

Visible source quotations and escapes:

The expression marks several fragments as `PROSE-ESCAPE`, saying they are exact source quotations retained where RSS lacks a primitive. These are not claimed as successful RSS expression:

- “If different bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one.”
- “A conjecture: the more useful representation is a partial order of possible reservations, not a set, because some alternatives may be compatible with others across bookings while others are not.”
- “A criticism: once you move to a set of possible worlds, you have smuggled in a notion of possibility that the original bag did not contain.”
- “So the first is better supported, but the second remains a live conjecture, especially if one thinks expired records are no longer \"delivered records\" in the relevant sense.”
- “That gives an interval, but intervals lose correlations: booking A's high alternative might be incompatible with booking B's high alternative if they share a physical resource not named in the snapshot.”
- “Does the absence of revision 6 matter? Not by the stated rules, but it might indicate a lost delivery.”
- “Does the snapshot represent the union of all deliveries, or the intersection, or one replica's view?”

There are also embedded translations or paraphrases not marked as exact source quotations, such as the statements about duplicate authority, higher revisions superseding lower ones, negative availability, or disagreement about uncertainty. These are interpretations. Even if they resemble source statements, their presence in the expression does not by itself establish that RSS carried the source content. Reconstruction from the PROSE-ESCAPE fragments uses ordinary prose, not RSS primitives.

So, under RSS, the expression is best read as an account-set or inquiry state: it preserves rival readings, conflicts, conjectures, and criticisms. Its RSS-native content is mainly the Viewpoint/Bag/Story/Conflict/Reading/Projection/Account machinery. Its claims about intervals, convexity, partial orders, possible worlds, evidential support, lost deliveries, and bag union/intersection are carried by prose escapes, not by the selected carrier. Its most substantive unresolved question is whether that hybrid is a faithful exposure of the source’s uncertainty or an over-permissive reconstruction that leaves operational decisions to later, possibly inconsistent, readers.

The expression is best read as a hybrid: an RSS-flavored account of the frozen warehouse prose, with seven explicit `PROSE-ESCAPE` fragments where RSS lacks primitives. It is not a single RSS formula, and it does not claim to be one. That is a legitimate disposition for the selected carrier. RSS is explicitly noncomputable and does not require a decision procedure, so the expression should not be faulted merely for failing to produce one. The more useful question is where the translation into RSS loses, adds, or hardens something relative to the frozen prose, and where the independent reading misstates the evidence.

The `PROSE-ESCAPE` quotations are exact against the frozen corpus. For example, the source has:

> “If different bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one.”

The expression quotes this exactly and marks the RSS obstruction correctly. The same is true of the partial-order conjecture, the possible-worlds criticism, the “better supported” sentence, the interval-correlation criticism, the lost-delivery sentence, and the union/intersection/single-replica-view question. So the escapes are not a fabrication or a paraphrase masquerading as quotation. That matters because the independent reading says, “The source quotations cannot be verified here because the source corpus field is withheld.” In this packet the corpus text is present, and the quotations can be verified. That is a defect in the probe or reader visibility, not in RSS or in the expression. The independent reading’s caution is therefore partly obsolete here.

The clearest lost distinction is the source’s assertion of shared coordinates. The source says:

> “The capacity and logical time are shared coordinates, but the records arrive as a bag…”

The expression instead says:

> “Take the described snapshot as a Viewpoint: a Coordinate (capacity, logical time) and a Bag of deliveries.”

Later the expression says:

> “different Viewpoints may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative—in RSS, viewpoint-relative.”

RSS defines a Coordinate as something that “can be shared or replica-relative” and treats coordinates as “parameters of a viewpoint, not as absolute facts.” So the expression’s move is RSS-native, but it weakens the source’s initial claim. A distinguishing case: two replicas have the same capacity and logical time but different bags. The source describes capacity and logical time as shared coordinates, so their sameness is part of the snapshot description. The expression’s Viewpoint framing permits their difference, and later explicitly contemplates different logical times across viewpoints. This is an introduced RSS commitment: coordinates are viewpoint parameters. It is not fatal, because RSS permits shared coordinates, but the expression does not preserve the source’s default. A proposed repair, not installed, would be to distinguish a shared coordinate from a viewpoint-relative coordinate, and to treat replica-relative time as a separate reading or conjecture rather than as the initial framing.

A second specific defect is the treatment of exact duplication. The source says:

> “Duplicate delivery of the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry adds nothing…”

The expression says:

> “Exact duplicate deliveries—same booking, revision, kind, quantity, expiry—add no authority…”

But RSS defines exact duplication as equality of “all record fields **and provenance**.” The expression uses the RSS term “Exact duplicate” while dropping the RSS provenance condition. A distinguishing case: two deliveries have the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry, but different provenance. Under the source’s wording, they are duplicates in the named fields and add no additional authority. Under RSS, they are not exact duplicates, because provenance differs. The expression’s phrasing therefore either narrows RSS or silently treats a source-level same-field duplicate as an RSS exact duplicate. This is a translator defect relative to the selected carrier, and the independent reading catches it. A repair would be to rename the source-level notion, for example “same-field duplicate,” and reserve “exact duplicate” for the RSS notion including provenance. That repair should be recorded, not installed.

A related but smaller loss is near-duplication. The source says:

> “if two records share booking and revision but differ in kind or quantity, are they duplicates or alternatives?”

The expression says:

> “two records sharing booking and revision but differing in kind or quantity are near-duplicates and candidates for Conflict…”

But RSS says near-duplication is when two deliveries “share booking and revision but differ in kind, quantity, **or expiry**.” The expression omits expiry. A distinguishing case: two records share booking and revision and have the same kind and quantity, but different expiry. The source’s exact-duplicate condition includes expiry, so they are not exact duplicates. RSS would call them near-duplicates. The expression’s paraphrase would not clearly classify them that way. This is a small but real lost distinction, and the repair is simply to include expiry in the near-duplicate description.

The next issue is supersession versus removal. The source says:

> “A higher revision kills lower revisions for that booking…”

and later:

> “group its records by revision, then keep only the greatest revision present.”

The expression repeats “supersedes” and “keeps only the greatest revision present.” RSS says supersession is “structural within a reading” and that lower revisions can remain in the Bag/Viewpoint as superseded stories. A distinguishing case is the one the source itself uses: revision 5 expired, revision 3 active. Under Reading A, revision 5 remains the chosen record but reserves zero, and revision 3 stays obsolete. Under Reading B, expiry deletes revision 5, so revision 3 becomes greatest and active. If “keeps only the greatest revision present” is read as removing lower revisions from the Bag, then Reading B cannot be represented as expiry deleting the high revision; one would have to restore the lower revision. The expression does preserve both readings as readings, so the defect is not total. But the phrase “keeps only” can blur the distinction between Bag membership and liveness/selection. The source itself uses that phrase, so the defect is partly inherited from the prose. Still, under RSS the translator should separate “remains in the Bag” from “is selected/live.” A proposed repair would be to say that lower revisions remain in the Bag but are superseded under Reading A, and that Reading B changes which record is treated as greatest by deleting or demoting the high revision.

Replication is another place where the translation substitutes an RSS primitive for a source notion. The source says:

> “It assumes logical current time is a single coordinate, but different replicas may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative.”

The expression says:

> “It assumes logical current time is a single Coordinate, but different Viewpoints may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative—in RSS, viewpoint-relative.”

RSS has no primitive for a replica. It has Viewpoints, Coordinates, Bags, Stories, Accounts, and Readings. A replica can be modeled as a Viewpoint, but not every Viewpoint is a replica. A distinguishing case: two observers with the same coordinate and the same bag but different trust in provenance are two Viewpoints but not two replicas. Conversely, two replicas that have merged identically might be one Viewpoint under discussion. The expression later flags the union/intersection/single-replica-view question as a `PROSE-ESCAPE`, which is the right move. But in the fourth disagreement it replaces “replica” with “Viewpoint” without marking that as a modeling assumption. This is a selected-language limitation: RSS lacks a replication primitive. It is not a failure of the source objection, and the prose escape keeps the objection admissible. A proposed repair would be to add an explicit modeling note or a relational primitive distinguishing replica from viewpoint, or to say “replica, modeled here as a Viewpoint.”

The expression’s handling of interval, convexity, partial order, possible worlds, evidential support, lost deliveries, and bag union/intersection is mostly honest. It marks them as `PROSE-ESCAPE` and states the RSS obstruction. This is exactly what the task permits: unsupported substantive content remains in ordinary prose. The selected carrier RSS does not have primitives for those notions, but that does not make the source’s objections impossible or inadmissible. It only means RSS cannot carry them as RSS relations. The expression does not falsely claim otherwise. The independent reading is right that the substantive criticism in those passages lives in prose, not in RSS, but that is not automatically a defect. It would become a defect only if the expression claimed those passages were RSS-native or if it dropped them. It does not.

There are several smaller introduced commitments. The expression says:

> “Availability is capacity minus whatever reservation is actually selected. In RSS, ‘actually’ signals a Reading.”

The source says:

> “Availability is then capacity minus whatever reservation is actually selected, but the word ‘actually’ hides the problem.”

Mapping “actually” to a Reading is RSS-native, but it may over-specify. A distinguishing case: someone might object not to the choice of expiry or tie-breaking policy, but to the assumption that there is a single actual selection at all. RSS can leave that as an open question, but the expression’s wording makes “Reading” the carrier of the problem. This is a mild over-assimilation rather than a lost distinction, because the expression later says no Reading is selected.

The expression also ends with:

> “this is not a failure of the reconstruction, but the only honest form the frozen text permits.”

The source ends with:

> “Keeping these disagreements visible is not a failure of the reconstruction; it is the reconstruction’s only honest form.”

The expression adds “the frozen text permits.” That is a normative attribution. The source’s claim is about the honesty of the reconstruction; the expression turns it into a claim about what the frozen text permits. RSS does not entail that the frozen text permits only this form. The independent reading flags this correctly. A repair would be to restore the source wording or to mark the sentence as a normative commitment rather than an RSS entailment.

The independent reading is otherwise largely accurate. It correctly identifies the main RSS-native machinery: Viewpoint, Coordinate, Bag, Story, Conflict, Reading, Projection, Account, Inquiry state. It correctly says no Reading is selected. It correctly notes that the expression treats negative availability as a signal, that it leaves release semantics open, that it leaves union/intersection/single-view open, and that it lacks a resource model. Its strongest criticisms are the provenance omission in exact duplication, the potential conflation of supersession with removal, and the substitution of Viewpoint for replica. Its weakest move is the claim that the source corpus is withheld; in this packet it is not. That is a probe/reader issue, not an RSS issue. Its claim that the final sentence is a normative commitment is also valid.

The defect loci can be summarized as follows. Translator defects: snapshot-to-Viewpoint substitution without preserving shared coordinates; exact-duplicate phrasing that drops RSS provenance; near-duplicate phrasing that drops expiry; possible blurring of Bag membership and supersession; and the added “frozen text permits” in the final sentence. Selected-language defects: RSS lacks primitives for replica, interval, convexity, partial order, possible worlds, evidential support, lost deliveries, and bag union/intersection. These are correctly marked as prose escapes, so they are not fatal to the expression. Reader/probe defects: the independent reading assumes the source is withheld and therefore cannot verify the `PROSE-ESCAPE` quotations, though they are exact in the packet. Compiler-bridge defects: none are evident; the expression is not claiming a Lean translation, and RSS is allowed to be noncomputable. The main bridge issue is that the expression sometimes uses RSS terms as labels for source-level notions that are not identical to RSS primitives, especially “exact duplicate.”

The unresolved disposition is that several competing readings remain live. On a charitable hybrid reading, the expression is a faithful exposure of the source’s uncertainty: it uses RSS where RSS can carry the content and prose escapes where it cannot. On a critical-limits reading, the expression shows that RSS is too weak for the warehouse problem: the substantive mathematical and replication content sits in the escapes, and RSS provides structure without deciding the hard cases. On an over-assimilation reading, the expression forces the source into RSS vocabulary and thereby introduces commitments about coordinates, duplicates, and readings that the source did not make. None of these readings is forced by the evidence. The proposed repairs are recorded but not installed: distinguish shared coordinates from viewpoint parameters; define same-field duplication separately from RSS exact duplication with provenance; include expiry in near-duplication; separate Bag membership from liveness; mark replica-to-Viewpoint substitution as a modeling assumption; and restore or qualify the final normative sentence. The source’s interval, convexity, partial-order, possible-worlds, support, lost-delivery, and bag-algebra objections remain admissible in ordinary prose even though RSS cannot encode them as RSS relations.
